blocks.value: Teacher waves with Pip. Child waves back before speaking — silent-period friendly.

blocks.label: My name is
blocks.subject: Pip pointing to own chest, introducing himself

blocks.label: Nice to meet you
blocks.subject: Pip and Bella shaking hands, both smiling

blocks.label: Two-character dialogue scene
blocks.subject: Pip the fox and Bella the bunny meeting, dual speech bubbles

blocks.label: Bella replies
blocks.text: Hi! My name is Bella. Nice to meet you!

blocks.label: Teacher notes
blocks.value: I-DO MODEL (ESA · Study): Play the Pip↔Bella dialogue 3× with exaggerated gestures — wave on 'Hello', point to chest on 'My name is', handshake mime on 'Nice to meet you'. Child stays silent and mimics gestures only. This honours the natural silent period while binding sound → gesture → meaning without translation.

blocks.label: Sentence frame
blocks.value: Hello! My name is ___. Nice to meet you!

blocks.label: Pip cues the child
blocks.text: Your turn! Hello! My name is...

blocks.label: Roleplay rotation
blocks.value: WE-DO → YOU-DO (ESA · Activate): Run a 3-turn roleplay circle. Child greets Pip, then Bella, then Charlie Chick — each NPC replies with a slightly different chunk (Hi! / Nice to meet you! / Hello friend!) so the child hears variation but always SAYS the same frame. Drag-match follows: Hello↔wave, Goodbye↔wave-away, My name is↔point-to-chest, Nice to meet you↔handshake. Align the 4 images as a centred 2×2 grid.

blocks.label: Teacher notes
blocks.value: Treat 'My name is ___' as ONE unanalysed lexical chunk (no grammar talk). Praise bravery > accuracy. If the child stays silent, Pip models again and the child only waves — that still counts as a turn.

blocks.label: Teacher notes
blocks.value: 60-second micro-moment only. Child puts a hand in front of the mouth to feel the puff of air on /h/. Pop the /h/ words as they appear. Do NOT extend into a full phonics lesson — that lives in L2/L3.

blocks.label: Teacher notes
blocks.value: FINE-MOTOR + EXIT-HIGH: Child traces lowercase 'h' once (down-stroke, then bump). Then Pip waves: 'Goodbye! See you next lesson!' — confetti + Vault sticker. NEVER end on a quiz; always exit on celebration.
